summary: Validated Iteration 10 (Layer 5 FIFA k-NN + Step 3 career_brief). All 13 existing pytests in test_archetype_4layer.py PASS plus 10 new independent tests in test_iter10_fifa_career.py — 9/10 pass on first run; the 10th (PDF) initially failed because a stale iter9-era PDF was cached at /app/backend/pdfs/{rid}.pdf. After cache removal, regenerated PDF includes FIFA DATA TWIN, CAREER SNAPSHOT, k-NN/similarity wording, and a 5-row table of percentages — all 10 new tests pass. Backend report payload confirmed: archetype.lenses.fifa present (label='FIFA data twin', similarity_pct≤92, score≤9.2, why mentions 7,473 pros), archetype.fifa_neighbors=5 sorted desc, archetype.fifa_db_meta.size>=7000, archetype.career_brief mentions Modric/Croatia/Ballon. Narrative (cache v3) regenerated and weaves career_brief or FIFA top match. 4 legacy lens scores (style/build/role/path) confirmed ≤10 — the iter9 lens-score-out-of-range bug is fixed. Frontend UI navigation from dashboard could not be automated (data-testid missing on dashboard report card links/buttons); however since the entire data contract is validated via backend and the rendered DOM testids on /reports/{rid} are produced server-side, main agent can self-verify by logging in manually.

minor.issue: Cached PDF at /app/backend/pdfs/{rid}.pdf is NOT invalidated when archetype.career_brief or archetype.fifa_neighbors changes. Existing premium users on Lukas's report will continue to receive the iter9-era PDF (no FIFA DATA TWIN / CAREER SNAPSHOT sections) until the file is manually removed or the report archetype hash changes. Recommended fix: include a content hash (e.g. archetype.id + len(neighbors) + career_brief[:32] + _NARRATIVE_CACHE_VERSION) in the cached PDF filename, or always regenerate when the on-disk hash mtime predates _NARRATIVE_CACHE_VERSION bump. Reproduction: GET /api/reports/{rid}/pdf returns 200 with stale content. Mitigation already applied for testing: rm /app/backend/pdfs/64f59196*.pdf.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'VIEW →' link on each report card does NOT use an <a href='/reports/...'> element and has no data-testid (e.g. data-testid='open-report-{rid}' or 'dashboard-report-{rid}'). Automated tests (and accessibility tools) cannot reliably target a single report card. Manual click works fine in a real browser.

action_items: Add a cache-busting hash (or invalidate by version) for /api/reports/{rid}/pdf so existing PDFs regenerate when career_brief/fifa_neighbors are added.
Add data-testid='open-report-{rid}' (or wrap the dashboard card in <Link to=`/reports/{rid}`>) so the dashboard→report navigation is testable and accessible.

Main agent can manually verify the frontend by logging in as premium@elitescout.com → opening Lukas A. → confirming archetype-career-brief, lens-match-fifa (forest bg, %), fifa-data-twin-panel + fifa-neighbor-0..4 testids are present and the narrative mentions Croatia / Ballon d'Or or the closest FIFA pro by name.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py PDF cache at /app/backend/pdfs/{rid}.pdf is not keyed by archetype/narrative version — stale PDFs persist across feature ships. This is the same class of bug as the narrative cache, which was fixed via _NARRATIVE_CACHE_VERSION.
DashboardPage report cards lack a data-testid on the clickable element, making any automated dashboard→report flow fragile.
server.py is now ~4700+ lines and still single-file. Splitting into modules (archetype/, reports/, pdf/, auth/, fifa/) remains warranted.
find_fifa_neighbors() correctly caps similarity at 92% — verified on live data (Lukas top match ~88%).

rca of the issue: Stale-PDF RCA: server.py's /api/reports/{rid}/pdf handler (~line 4097) caches the rendered PDF at PDF_DIR / f'{report_id}.pdf' and returns the cached file when pdf_path.exists(). The cache key is purely the report_id — it does NOT include _NARRATIVE_CACHE_VERSION, archetype hash, or a feature-version tag. When iteration 10 added FIFA DATA TWIN + CAREER SNAPSHOT sections to _archetype_card_pdf() / _lens_matches_pdf() / new _fifa_neighbors_pdf(), existing on-disk PDFs were left untouched and continue to be served. Reproduction: download the Lukas PDF on a fresh paid account → see iter9-style PDF (no FIFA section) → rm /app/backend/pdfs/{rid}.pdf → re-download → new content appears. Fix: name the cache file by hash of (report_id + _NARRATIVE_CACHE_VERSION + archetype.id + len(fifa_neighbors) + len(career_brief or '')) so any backend feature ship auto-invalidates.
